title: raglab context payload
description: Hand-off contract between the retrieval layer and any consuming application. spec_version follows semver; consumers pin against it.

spec_version.description: 1.0.0 (single probe), 1.1.0 (adds doc_type on sources and the composed fields), or 1.2.0 (adds provenance on every chunk); every earlier field unchanged

query.description: The question exactly as the caller asked it.

status.description: Decided upstream, never by the consumer: ok = evidence served; insufficient_evidence = the corpus could not support an answer (say so); out_of_scope = outside the corpus's domain (relay boundary_response).

confidence.description: Best reranker score. Informs the consumer; does not authorize. Absent on out_of_scope.

boundary_response.description: Definitive corpus-boundary statement. Present only on out_of_scope; the consumer relays it verbatim.

retrieved_at.description: UTC timestamp of the retrieval, ISO 8601.

years.description: Plan years searched (an event source is exempt from the year filter).

plan_codes.description: Plan codes searched; empty = every plan the caller may see.

router.description: What the platform actually searched — the routed plan years and plan codes, the as-of date for versioned sources, and whether the plan came from the member's enrollment — never what a model guessed.

text.description: The chunk as delivered: the document text with its context prefix; PHI already pseudonymized at ingest.

path.description: Source file path relative to the corpus root.

plan_code.description: Plan code the document belongs to; null for documents that are not plan-specific.

year.description: Plan year of the document (issue year for event sources).

pages.description: Page numbers the chunk spans (cite these).

section.description: Section heading the chunk sits under.

content_hash.description: Source document fingerprint (bytes + processing recipe): lineage to the exact version retrieved.

record.description: For member records: the record system's required fields (case id, claim id, call id, dates, codes) — metadata, never extracted from text.

doc_type.description: Source type from the registry: brochure, carrier_letter, clinical_policy, bulletin, sop, formulary, kb, rates, call_note, appeal, clinical_note.

source.description: Where the text came from: enough to cite it and to identify the exact document version.

provenance.description: Reproducibility facts (spec 1.2.0): the document version label read from governed metadata, the processing recipe that produced the document, and the model that embedded the chunk. null recipe/model = ingested before provenance was recorded.

document_version.description: A version label read from governed metadata (policy version and effective date, letter or bulletin id, plan year, record date, or the plan-year edition) — what a person says out loud; content_hash is the exact identity.

recipe.description: The processing recipe that produced the document: parser, chunk limits, contextual mode, de-identification mode and version, search-copy dictionary. Compare with the current corpus before re-running anything.

embedding_model.description: The model that embedded this chunk; a query must be embedded by the same model to be comparable.

acl_basis.description: The ACL tier that entitled the caller to this chunk.

rrf.description: Reciprocal-rank-fusion score from the hybrid (vector + lexical) search.

rerank.description: Cross-encoder reranker score, 0–1; the abstention threshold is applied to the best of these.

chunks.description: The evidence, ranked by the reranker; each entry is a self-contained citation unit.

payload_id.description: UUID; joins to the disclosure log.

persona.description: The document-lane persona the retrieval ran as (the row-level-security role).

member_context.description: The member key the retrieval was scoped to, when a member context was supplied; null otherwise.

record_context.description: The record fields bound from identifiers in the question or the surface (case id, claim id, policy id): filters, never search words.

kind.description: Identifier kind: member_id, mrn, claim_id, case_id, policy_id, bulletin_id.

unresolved_identifiers.description: Well-formed identifiers (shape + check digit) that match no record: the caller typed an ID that exists for nobody

as_of_defaulted.description: True when a policy leg ran with today's date because no claim in the question supplied a date of service

subject.description: The member ID this context is about, when member-scoped (masked by role at the surface)

shape.description: simple = one document probe; compound = several legs composed under one status.

origin.description: Who produced the plan: rules (the platform's structural rules), caller (the surface supplied it), model (the planner model proposed it and the platform validated it).

widened.description: True when the platform widened the plan beyond what was proposed (e.g. a document leg added to a warehouse-only question).

model.description: The planner model used, or null when no model call was made.

name.description: Leg name; sub_results and warehouse_results refer to it.

kind.description: doc_probe = a search over the governed document corpus; member_query = a named warehouse query.

text.description: For a document leg: the search text the platform ran (identifiers resolved, not searched).

sources.description: For a document leg: the source types it was narrowed to; empty = every source the caller may see.

query_name.description: For a warehouse leg: the named query from the catalog.

slots.description: For a warehouse leg: the parameters the platform bound (member_id, claim_id, case_id …).

required.description: True = this leg must return evidence for the payload to be ok; false = best-effort.

legs.description: The legs, in the order they ran.

plan.description: What the platform decided to look at for this question: the shape, who decided, and the legs it ran (at most three, one pass, no chaining).

status.description: The leg's own status; not_executed = the platform could not run it (no member context, no entitlement).

confidence.description: Best reranker score for this leg.

reason.description: Why a leg did not return evidence, in words.

router.description: The route this leg searched (years, plan_codes, as_of).

chunk_indexes.description: Indexes into chunks[] that this leg contributed.

widened.description: True when the leg's route was widened (e.g. every version of a policy for a change question).

sub_results.description: One entry per document leg: what it returned.

status.description: ok = rows returned; insufficient_evidence = no rows; not_executed = the leg could not run (no warehouse identity, no bound parameter); unknown_query = not in the catalog.

reason.description: Why the leg returned nothing, in words.

rows.description: Rows as arrays aligned to columns; values in masked_columns are policy-masked, not absent.

masked_columns.description: Columns the warehouse masked for this role — report them as 'not visible to your role'; a null elsewhere is genuinely absent data.

warehouse_results.description: One entry per warehouse leg: the rows the named query returned as the caller's warehouse role.

missing.description: Required legs that did not return evidence (worst-of-required)

field.description: The metadata level the rule expanded (e.g. plan_code).

asked.description: The level the question named (e.g. the program).

keys.description: Every key beneath that was searched.

in_corpus.description: Keys the corpus holds documents for.

with_evidence.description: Keys that contributed evidence to this payload.

not_offered.description: keys the registry declares as not offered in the routed years

level.description: which level the question named: program (plans beneath covered) or option (programs above covered)

missing_from_corpus.description: Keys the registry declares but the corpus lacks — the consumer should say these were not covered.

coverage.description: The coverage rule fired: the question named a level (e.g. a program) but not the level beneath (its plans); every key beneath was searched — which have evidence here, which the corpus lacks

search.description: How much searching the question needed: readings = sub-searches run (one per covered plan, routed year, or policy version); candidates = the merged pool the reranker scored; trimmed = candidates cut by the cap. More ambiguity means more readings and more time.

readings.description: Sub-searches run: one per covered plan, routed year, or policy version.

candidates.description: Size of the merged candidate pool the reranker scored.

trimmed.description: Candidates cut by the cap before reranking.
